events.name: A Birthday Tribute to John Coltrane with Derek Douget, Ricardo Pascal & Trevarri
events.info: A Birthday Tribute to John ColtraneCelebrate the music and legacy of one of the most influential and innovative figures in jazz with a special birthday tribute to John Coltrane. Leading the performance is Derek Douget, a celebrated saxophonist whose music is deeply rooted in the rich, multicultural traditions of Louisiana. Raised in Gonzales, Douget began playing saxophone at age 10 and went on to be mentored by Ellis Marsalis and Harold Battiste. His career includes performances and recordings with Nicholas Payton, Terence Blanchard, Ellis Marsalis, the New Orleans Jazz Orchestra, Maurice Brown and more, including the Grammy-winning Book One. This perfomance brings together 2 additional outstanding New Orleans based saxophonists---Ricardo Pascal, and Trevarri Huff-Boone---to honor Coltrane's enduring influence and extraordinary musical legacy. From Coltrane's groundbreaking work in bebop, hard bop, and modal jazz to his later explorations of spirituality and free improvisation, Coltrane continually expanded the possibilities of jazz and inspired generations of musicians. Derek Douget, Ricardo Pascal, and Trevarri Huff-Boone each bring their own distinctive voices and perspectives to Coltrane's compositions, promising an evening of powerful melodies, deep grooves, adventurous improvisation, and the spirit of musical exploration that defined Coltrane's career. Join us at Snug Harbor Jazz Bistro for a special celebration of John Coltrane's music and legacy. This event is co-sponsored by NOLA x NOLA and features: Derek Douget - saxophone Ricardo Pascal - saxophone Trevarri - saxophone Jason Marsalis - drums Dwight Fitch - piano Jason Stewart - bass Shows at 7:30pm & 9:30pm Doors at 7pm & 9pm Restaurant is Open 5pm - 10pm for dinner before or after your showtime: Advance Ticket Holders can now automatically make dinner table reservations for the Dining Room online via OpenTable.com ! Advance Ticket-Holders can also make table reservations for dinner by Emailing reservations@snugjazz.com after your tickets have been purchased online. Dinner Service without Advance Concert Tickets is first-come, first-served based on availability upon arrival. Kind Reminder: Snug Harbor does NOT serve the full menu inside the Music Room. We do offer cheese and charcuterie tray options. In order to preserve the integrity, quiet and focus of our world class intimate concerts, only the charcuterie, cocktails and soft drinks are available for table service inside the Music Room. However, we encourage you to arrive at least 90 Minutes prior to your showtime in order to enjoy full, relaxing dinner service in the Dining Room right next door, before getting seated in the Music Room for your ticketed showtime.

Sam Kuslan is a New Orleans singer, pianist, arranger, and musical director known for his soulful voice, lush piano playing, and energetic stage presence. Inspired by the Great American Songbook and New Orleans. He blends jazz, pop, funk, and contemporary influences. Praised by OffBeat Magazine for his , "rdquo" -> New Orleans masters--style piano," Kuslan has toured extensively throughout the U.S. and Europe, performing with Naughty Professor, Sean McConnell, and the National Park Service Centennial Band. events.name: Damien Jurado with St. Yuma
events.info: Play on, theres no such thing as better days, Damien Jurado sings on Roger, the sweeping wash of a song that opens Reggae Film Star, his 18th full length album and second release from Jurados own Maraqopa Records label. But as he enters his 25th year as a recording artist, its clear these are, at the least, very good days for Jurado on the creative front. In these 12 songs, which evoke half-recalled dreams and overheard conversations, the cosmic rushes headlong into the autobiographical and specific moments on the clock fade from past to future to scenes set only in the eternal now. Playing out like a backlot documentary filmed on the location of an unnamed TV or film setmaybe a sitcom taping, or perhaps its a low budget science fiction B-movie, or could it be a talk show?the album is populated by performers awaiting call times, camera operators praying for their shot, and studio audiences rapt with anticipation. The stars here eschew glitz and glamor. Instead, they wander grocery stores and parking lots in the verdant Pacific Northwest and the desert Southwest, looking for payphones and a sense of purpose. Produced by Jurado with multi-instrumentalist Josh Gordon and recording engineer Alex Bush at Sonikwire studio in Irvine,CA, Jurados home away from home and musical headquarters, the records compositions are among the most musically rich in his vast discography, encompassing romantic AM gold, 60s psychedelia, driving rock s unmistakable voice, at once intimately present and ghostly, grounded in the here and now but capable, at any moment, of drifting off into the divinatory. Following threads established by 2021s The Monster Who Hated Pennsylvania, the album sees Jurado embracing his auteur era, penning vignettes that arrive with little fanfare and depart quicker than you might suspect, only to linger long after they wrap. Seeking a skeleton key to decipher the action is beside the pointJurados songs are worlds meant to be lived in, not picked apartbut on the beatific single What Happened To The Class Of 65? the singer imagines himself as both the viewer and the viewed, the eye behind the camera and its subject. This emotional and spiritual transference animates Reggae Film Star. Like a masterful director, Jurado offers motivation to the listener, staring unblinkingly from the mise-en-scne in your mind. Look into the camera, he commands on The Day Of The Robot, One more time with anger/And sadness/I believe you. A quarter-century in, Jurado remains gripped by his visions and driven by an unmatched creative drive. Reggae Film Star is one of Damien Jurados finest works to date, a stunning new feature from one of indie rocks most cinematic figures. Here on this sound stage, you are the camera, you are the scene, you are the setting, and you are the viewer. Please try not to blink.-Jason P. Woodbury

events.name: The First Course: Elevated Dining presented by AT&T, Moet, & Veuve Clicquot
events.description:
Before the gates open and the 10th anniversary weekend officially begins, experience the National Fried Chicken Festival like never before.

Join us Thursday, October 1, from 6–9 PM for The First Course, an intimate chicken and champagne dinner beneath the stars on the New Orleans Lakefront. Created as an elevated opening to the Festival’s 10th-anniversary celebration, this one-night-only experience brings together acclaimed culinary talent, premium champagne and live entertainment for an unforgettable evening on the festival grounds.

Guests will enjoy a four-course, chef-crafted dinner, with each course showcasing the distinctive style and creativity of a featured chef:

Vlad Kogan, Executive Chef, The Windsor Court
Allison Birdsall, Executive Chef, Rosedale
Edgar “Dook” Chase IV, Renowned Restaurateur & Chef
Jeremy Fogg, Acclaimed Pastry Chef

Each course will be thoughtfully complemented by premium Moët & Veuve Clicquot champagne pairings, creating a dining experience designed to celebrate the many possibilities of chicken and champagne.

As the evening unfolds, enjoy live entertainment and dancing beneath the stars, along with an exclusive sneak peek of the National Fried Chicken Festival grounds before gates officially open to the public on Friday.

Elegant, intimate and created exclusively for the Festival’s milestone anniversary, The First Course is your invitation to experience a different side of the National Fried Chicken Festival—and raise a glass to the weekend ahead.

Seating for this exclusive experience is extremely limited. Secure your place at the table while reservations remain.

events.info: Revisited: The Early Days of Snug HarborTake a trip down memory lane and revisit the beginnings of Snug Harbor's dynamic legacy. events.name: Pete Murano Band featuring Noah Young, Cam Watson & more
events.info: Pete Murano was raised all across America. Born in the Northeast, he moved to St. Louis and finally settled in New Orleans, Louisiana. In 2003, Murano joined forces with Trombone Shorty & Orleans Avenue. Here, he developed a sound that was all his own, combining elements of rock, funk, and R&B. With Shorty, Murano has written, recorded, and toured the world extensively. His sound on guitar is often raw and distorted, yet soulful. Now, on his first solo release, he embraces that sound as it vibrates into the world. On October 1st, hell be joined by bassist Noah Young (Naughty Professor), Cam Watson (Jon Batiste) on keys, and more.

Led by master pianist and composer Lawrence Sieberth and featuring a stunning projection-mapping light show by artist Monica Kelly, this special presentation brings together music, visuals, and memories from Snug Harbor's rich history. Expect an evening of remarkable musicianship and timeless jazz featuring some of our most treasured all-stars, along with appearances by several very special guests. This presentation is co-sponsored by NOLAxNOLA and features: House Band Lawrence Sieberth -- piano Tony DaGradi -- saxophones Steve Masakowski -- guitar Chris Severin -- bass Ricky Sebastian -- drums Special Guests Davell Crawford - vocals, piano Roger Lewis -- baritone saxophone Charmaine Neville -- vocals Oscar Rossignoli -- piano Betty Shirley -- vocals Shows at 7:30pm & 9:30pm Doors at 7pm & 9pm Restaurant is Open 5pm - 10pm for dinner before or after your showtime: Advance Ticket Holders can now automatically make dinner table reservations for the Dining Room online via OpenTable.com ! Advance Ticket-Holders can also make table reservations for dinner by Emailing reservations@snugjazz.com after your tickets have been purchased online. Dinner Service without Advance Concert Tickets is first-come, first-served based on availability upon arrival. Kind Reminder: Snug Harbor does NOT serve the full menu inside the Music Room. We do offer cheese and charcuterie tray options. In order to preserve the integrity, quiet and focus of our world class intimate concerts, only the charcuterie, cocktails and soft drinks are available for table service inside the Music Room. However, we encourage you to arrive at least 90 Minutes prior to your showtime in order to enjoy full, relaxing dinner service in the Dining Room right next door, before getting seated in the Music Room for your ticketed showtime.

events.name: THE NATIONAL FRIED CHICKEN FESTIVAL PRESENTED BY RAISING CANE’S
events.description:
Ten years. Three days. One legendary city. This is the National Fried Chicken Festival.


Celebrate a decade of the National Fried Chicken Festival (FCF) presented by Raising Cane’s this fall along the scenic backdrop of the New Orleans Lakefront. Founded in 2016, FCF was built on a simple idea: bringing people together through a shared love of food. 

Now, for its 10th anniversary, the festival is going bigger than ever before with a three-day celebration and upgraded music lineup, featuring top-tier national recording artists throughout the weekend.

Come experience three full days of food, music, and culture, with delicious dishes from over 40 restaurants, three stages of entertainment featuring headline performances from Nelly, Dillon Francis, 2 Chainz, Keri Hilson, A-Trak, Ying Yang Twins, Webbie, Big Freedia + the Louisiana Philharmonic Orchestra, Marc Broussard, and many more, plus five unique lounge experiences, and fun for the whole family. From award-winning fried chicken favorites to vegetarian, vegan, and everything in between, FCF 2026 will showcase flavors for every palate.

Whether you're a longtime fan or experiencing the festival for the first time, don't miss the biggest celebration yet.

TICKET PRICING

Friday tickets are offered at past years’ price points, while Saturday and Sunday pricing reflects the expanded entertainment and featured performances on those days. Explore discounted weekend pass options and be sure to purchase early to lock in the lowest available price, as all tickets will continue to increase incrementally closer to the event:

**AS ALWAYS, KIDS 12 & UNDER GET IN FREE**

FOR GA: All kids must be with a ticketed adult. No more than two kids per ticketed adult.

FOR VIP: Anyone under the age of 21 will require an Accompanying Minor VIP ticket to enter the All-Ages VIP Lounges with a VIP-ticketed adult.

PARKING ADD-ON: New this year, you can now skip the hassle of paying on-site and pre-purchase parking as an add-on to any ticket.
